questions.question_text: List all the prime numbers between 10 and 20. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The prime numbers between 10 and 20 are 11, 13, 17, and 19 because they have exactly two distinct factors.

questions.question_text: Define intersecting lines and give one real-life example. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Intersecting lines are two lines that cross each other at exactly one point. A common real-life example is the crossing blades of a pair of scissors.

questions.question_text: Find the general rule for the pattern: 5, 10, 15, 20... where 'n' is the position. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The pattern increases by 5 each time. Therefore, the general mathematical rule for this sequence is 5n, where n is the position.

questions.question_text: Determine if 534 is divisible by 3 using the divisibility rule. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The sum of the digits is 5 plus 3 plus 4, which equals 12. Since 12 is divisible by 3, the number 534 is also divisible by 3.

questions.question_text: What is a reflex angle? State its measurement range. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A reflex angle is an angle that is greater than 180 degrees but strictly less than a complete turn of 360 degrees.

questions.question_text: Express 36 as the sum of two odd prime numbers. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: To express 36 as a sum of two odd primes, we can use 17 and 19, or 5 and 31. Let's use 17 + 19 = 36.

questions.question_text: Find the prime factorization of 120 using the factor tree method. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Starting with 120, divide by the smallest prime, 2, to get 60. Divide 60 by 2 to get 30. Divide 30 by 2 to get 15. Finally, divide 15 by 3 to get 5. The prime factorization is 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5.

questions.question_text: A class has 40 students. In a survey about favorite fruits, 12 chose Mango, 10 chose Apple, 8 chose Banana, and the rest chose Orange. How many chose Orange, and how would you represent this on a tally chart? [40-50 words]
questions.answer: First, sum the known choices: 12 plus 10 plus 8 equals 30. Subtract 30 from 40 to find that 10 students chose Orange. On a tally chart, Orange would be represented by two full blocks of five tally marks (four vertical lines crossed by one diagonal line, twice).

questions.question_text: Two angles form a linear pair. If one angle measures 65 degrees, find the measure of the other angle and explain your reasoning. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Angles in a linear pair add up to 180 degrees, forming a straight line. To find the unknown angle, subtract 65 degrees from 180 degrees, which gives exactly 115 degrees as the measure of the second angle.

questions.question_text: Find the greatest common divisor (HCF) of 24, 36, and 48 using prime factorization. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: First, find the prime factors: 24 is 2x2x2x3, 36 is 2x2x3x3, and 48 is 2x2x2x2x3. The common prime factors in all three numbers are two 2s and one 3. Multiplying these common factors gives 2 x 2 x 3, which equals an HCF of 12.

questions.question_text: A pattern is formed using matchsticks to make squares. 1 square needs 4 sticks, 2 joined squares need 7 sticks, 3 need 10 sticks. Find the rule for 'n' joined squares and calculate sticks for 10 squares. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The pattern sequence is 4, 7, 10. The difference is 3. The rule is 3n + 1, where n is the number of squares. For 10 joined squares, substitute n = 10 into the rule: 3(10) + 1, which equals 30 + 1. Therefore, 31 matchsticks are needed.

questions.question_text: In a geometry figure, two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one interior angle measures 110 degrees, what are the measures of the corresponding angle and the alternate interior angle? [40-50 words]
questions.answer: When parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal. Therefore, the corresponding angle measures exactly 110 degrees. Similarly, alternate interior angles are also equal, so the alternate interior angle will also measure exactly 110 degrees.

questions.question_text: Determine the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 15, 20, and 30 using the division method. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Arrange 15, 20, 30. Divide by 2: 15, 10, 15. Divide by 2 again: 15, 5, 15. Divide by 3: 5, 5, 5. Finally, divide by 5 to get 1, 1, 1. The LCM is the product of divisors: 2 x 2 x 3 x 5, which equals 60.

questions.question_text: Draw a rough sketch of an acute angle and an obtuse angle sharing a common vertex and one common arm. State what kind of angle is formed if their sum is exactly 90 degrees. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The sketch should show a common point (vertex) with a middle line (arm). If the sum of these two adjacent angles equals exactly 90 degrees, they are complementary angles, and together they form a perfect right angle. Note: an obtuse and acute angle cannot sum to 90.

questions.question_text: The students of Class 6 collected data on their preferred modes of transport to school: Bus (15), Car (8), Bicycle (12), Walking (5). Construct a well-labeled bar graph to represent this data. Assume a scale of 1 unit length = 2 students. Explain the steps. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: First, draw a horizontal x-axis labeled 'Modes of Transport' and mark Bus, Car, Bicycle, and Walking. Draw a vertical y-axis labeled 'Number of Students'. Using the scale 1 unit = 2 students, mark the y-axis (0, 2, 4, 6... up to 16). For the Bus, draw a bar up to halfway between 14 and 16 (height 7.5 units). For Car, draw a bar up to 8 (height 4 units). For Bicycle, draw a bar up to 12 (height 6 units). For Walking, draw a bar up to halfway between 4 and 6 (height 2.5 units). Ensure all bars have equal width and spacing.

questions.question_text: Three bells toll at intervals of 12 minutes, 15 minutes, and 20 minutes respectively. If they all tolled together at 8:00 AM, at what time will they next toll together again? Show all calculation steps clearly. [50-70 words]
questions.answer: To find when the bells toll together again, we must calculate the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of their intervals: 12, 15, and 20. The prime factorization is: 12 = 2x2x3; 15 = 3x5; 20 = 2x2x5. The LCM is the highest power of each prime factor: 2x2x3x5 = 60. Therefore, the bells will toll together after exactly 60 minutes. Since 60 minutes equals 1 hour, and they first tolled at 8:00 AM, they will toll together again exactly at 9:00 AM.

questions.question_text: Using a ruler and a compass, clearly outline the step-by-step process to construct an angle of 60 degrees, and then immediately construct its angle bisector to obtain a 30-degree angle. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: Step 1: Draw a straight ray OA. Step 2: With O as the center and any convenient radius, draw an arc intersecting OA at point B. Step 3: With B as the center and the same radius, draw another arc cutting the first arc at point C. Step 4: Draw a ray OD passing through C; angle DOA is now 60 degrees. Step 5: To bisect, use B and C as centers to draw two intersecting arcs inside the angle, meeting at point E. Step 6: Draw ray OE. Angle EOA is exactly 30 degrees.

questions.question_text: A teacher wants to distribute 108 notebooks, 144 pencils, and 180 erasers equally among her students such that no items are left over. What is the maximum number of students who can receive these items? How many of each item will each student get? [60-80 words]
questions.answer: To find the maximum number of students, calculate the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 108, 144, and 180. The prime factorizations are: 108 = 2x2x3x3x3; 144 = 2x2x2x2x3x3; 180 = 2x2x3x3x5. The common factors are 2x2x3x3, which equals 36. So, the maximum number of students is 36. To find the items per student, divide the total of each item by 36. Notebooks: 108 divided by 36 equals 3. Pencils: 144 divided by 36 equals 4. Erasers: 180 divided by 36 equals 5. Each student gets 3 notebooks, 4 pencils, and 5 erasers.
